Money

Pass the price and compare-at price as Money, the same { amount, currencyCode } shape Shopify’s Storefront API returns. A compare-at price that isn’t higher is ignored, so a data mistake never shows a fake sale.

Price is the one component every storefront block uses to show money. It takes a Money value, { amount: "48.00", currencyCode: "USD" }, and formats it with Intl for the shopper’s locale: $48.00 in the US, 48,00 € in Germany, ¥7,200 in Japan with no decimals, ₹4,000 with Indian grouping.
Prices for a storefront in any currency and locale. Handles sales, ranges, unit prices, free items and prices that change with the variant.

Show the price per 100 mL or per kg under the price, as EU rules require for goods sold by volume or weight. The money helpers do the math in minor units, so totals never drift.
Stripe, Paddle and most payment APIs send integers in the currency’s smallest unit. fromMinorUnits turns 4800 USD into $48.00 and 4800 JPY into ¥4,800, because yen has no cents.

The money helpers behind it, money, addMoney, multiplyMoney, sumMoney, fromMinorUnits and discountPercent, work in integer minor units so 0.1 + 0.2 is 0.30, and they refuse to add two currencies together. Cart, checkout and dashboard blocks use the same helpers.

When the price changes, for example when a shopper picks a bigger size, only the digits that changed roll to their new value, with tabular figures so nothing around the price moves. Unit prices sit on their own line under the price.
